quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?

options.text: Large vehicles need more distance to stop.
Large vehicles need less distance to stop.
Large vehicles make less noise.
Large vehicles travel faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large vehicles need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where you can see the traffic ahead.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level above the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. You cannot drink and drive safely.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line in the middle. What does this tell you?

options.text: Traffic flows in both directions on this road.
Traffic flows in only one direction on this road.
The road is being repaired.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows in both directions on this road.
questions.explanation: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: How can you avoid the risk of a crash caused by drunk driving?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say no to a drink by saying, "I'm driving."
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The only way to avoid the risks of drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, so it will be harder to make safe choices after you start drinking.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.
No turning allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Do not make a right turn at this location.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: When you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
When you slow down, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on wet pavement, the less your tires can remove water from the road. If you go too fast, your tires lose grip and you hydroplane, or slide on water.

questions.question: Is night driving more or less dangerous than day driving?

options.text: Less dangerous.
Just as dangerous.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. You cannot see as well in the dark. Other vehicles' headlights can blind you. More tired or impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is ahead. Watch for children.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private driveway?

options.text: Blow your horn to warn other drivers.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge with traffic.
Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When you enter a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.question: When you come to an accident scene, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your focus on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Focus on your driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to accident scenes just to look.

questions.question: When must you always use your turn signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. This includes changing lanes, pulling into traffic from a parking space, and passing another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a travel lane?

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you miss a freeway entrance ramp.
Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep driving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Drive to the next turn or exit instead.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in someone else's blind spot. Move ahead or fall back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights ahead. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down. If possible, change lanes so you will not drive next to the stopped emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.
Speed up to quickly pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If possible, change lanes so you will not drive next to the stopped emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you approach an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. Change lanes if you can do so safely to give the vehicle extra space. If changing lanes is unsafe, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to stop at a railroad crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
Stop your vehicle immediately and block their path.
Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
Signal to the emergency vehicle when it is safe for them to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
questions.explanation: Do everything you can to let an emergency vehicle with flashing lights pass. If it is safe, pull your vehicle to the side of the road to give them an open pathway.

questions.question: You approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Prepare to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed slowly and carefully. Look both ways before crossing.

questions.question: Traffic signals at an intersection are not working due to a power outage. What should you do?

options.text: Park your vehicle as far off the road as possible and wait for power to be restored.
Use hand signals to indicate your intentions to other drivers.
Turn on your hazard lights and proceed through the intersection without stopping.
Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When traffic lights are not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers and proceed through with caution when it is your turn.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Only if there is no oncoming traffic.
Only if the vehicle ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed. You cannot cross them to pass another vehicle. You may only cross them when turning into or out of a driveway or business entrance.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn but you are in the wrong lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and make your turn there.
Safely change lanes and put your vehicle in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and make your turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the proper lane, drive to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane there.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your vehicle's antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
It is best to use snow tires on your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter driving is difficult and requires extra caution. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line separating traffic mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. A dashed white line means you can cross it to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: When you see a green traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Continue driving unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection pass first. You may go, but drive at a safe speed so you can stop if the light changes.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival is very unlikely. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may take risky actions to pass you.
